messages:
deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.21-1678 deployed to prod-us (canary->100%). Post-deploy quick-check kicked off: convo-probe (simulated chat flows) + health pings.
Elaine: looking at convo-probe for us-central — p95 jumped sharply ~2m after deploy. p50 unchanged. No obvious errors in logs.
Elaine: snippet:
```
convo-probe region=us-central
p50  140ms
p95  520ms
p99 1600ms
errors 0 / 10000
seq_len distribution shifted: mode 64 -> 128
```
Samir: interesting — did we change the prompt templates or tokenization for generation-v3?
Nora: nothing on tokenizer. Release only touched runtime kernel selection (kernel-v3) and a batching tweak.
Miguel: sounds like a tail-latency regression from kernel-v3 under mid-long sequences. Recommend temporary route override for us-central to stable variant (stable-2026-03-20) while we investigate.
Elaine: +1. Also can we enable detailed traces for requests with seq > 200 so we get KV/cache footprints?
Miguel: @deploy-bot please execute: route-override region=us-central target=stable-2026-03-20 scope=runtime-routing
deploy-bot: executing route-override...
deploy-bot: route override applied for us-central -> stable-2026-03-20 (effective ts=1769332140). Affected pools: gpu-pool-usc-1,gpu-pool-usc-2.
oncall-bot: post-override quick health: convo-probe p95 back to 190ms within ~30s, p99 down to 420ms. error-budget delta +0.02%.
Samir: assigning follow-ups: @Miguel (perf/runtime bench) and @Nora (regression ticket + traces).
Nora: opened INF-5123 with attached probe traces and sample payloads: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5123
Miguel: I'll run micro-bench of kernel-v3 on a staging pool with sequences {64,128,256} and compare KV cache miss patterns, will post results in this thread.
Elaine: marking release as "partial pinned: us-central" and updating release notes + telling product ops. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: summary: partial routing override applied -> stable variant for us-central at 1769332140; synthetic convo probe recovered. Follow-ups: INF-5123, perf bench, decision before next roll. Closing this thread unless new regressions seen.
